name: Italy
cuisine_summary: Italian food is regional and ingredient-driven — long, slow Sundays of fresh pasta, wood-fired pizzas, and tomato sauces that taste like the tomato.
dish1_desc: Pasta tossed with pecorino and black pepper — three ingredients, all about technique.
dish2_desc: Tomato, mozzarella, basil on a charred, chewy crust. The standard everything else gets measured against.
dish3_desc: Espresso-soaked ladyfingers layered with sweet mascarpone — Italy's answer to coffee dessert.

name: France
cuisine_summary: Classic French cooking is patient and buttery — long lunches with crusty bread, sauces that took an afternoon, and dessert you crack with a spoon.
dish1_desc: Grilled steak with crispy fries — the bistro lunch staple. Order it medium-rare.
dish2_desc: Open-faced ham and gruyère sandwich, finished under the broiler with béchamel.
dish3_desc: Vanilla custard with a torched sugar crust you crack with the back of a spoon.

name: Spain
cuisine_summary: Spanish food is small plates and long evenings — sherry-paired tapas, cured ham sliced paper-thin, and rice cooked in a wide pan over fire.
dish1_desc: Fried potatoes with smoky tomato sauce and garlic aioli. Bar food, perfected.
dish2_desc: Dry-cured ham from acorn-fed pigs, sliced thin enough to melt on your tongue.
dish3_desc: Saffron rice cooked over fire with seafood or chicken. The crusty bottom (socarrat) is the prize.

name: Mexico
cuisine_summary: Mexican food in SF is more regional than the burrito stereotype — tacos al pastor off a vertical spit, mole that took two days, and salsas with real heat.
dish1_desc: Slow-cooked pork shoulder, crisped and piled into corn tortillas with onion and cilantro.
dish2_desc: Hominy stew with pork in a chile broth — garnish-your-own with cabbage, radish, lime.
dish3_desc: Roasted poblano peppers stuffed with cheese, dipped in egg batter, and fried golden.

name: Peru
cuisine_summary: Peruvian food fuses indigenous, Spanish, Chinese, and Japanese influences — bright citrus-cured ceviche, stir-fried beef over fries, and creamy chicken stews.
dish1_desc: Beef stir-fried with onions, tomato, and soy sauce — served over rice with fries. The Peru-China crossover hit.
dish2_desc: Raw white fish cured in lime, chile, and red onion. Cold, bright, addictive.
dish3_desc: Shredded chicken in a creamy aji amarillo sauce, served over rice and potato.

name: Argentina
cuisine_summary: Argentine cooking is wood smoke and beef — grilled meats with chimichurri, baked savory hand pies, and a wine country sensibility on the side.
dish1_desc: Hand pies stuffed with seasoned beef, chicken, or cheese. Baked, not fried — the everyday Argentine snack.
dish2_desc: Mixed grill of beef cuts, sausages, and offal. The Sunday family ritual.
dish3_desc: Bright herbaceous sauce of parsley, garlic, vinegar, and oil — the steak's required companion.

name: China
cuisine_summary: Chinese food in SF spans regions and eras — dim sum carts in Chinatown, soup dumplings folded with 18 pleats, and Sichuan numbing-hot chiles that buzz the lips.
dish1_desc: Shanghai soup dumplings — bite the side, sip the broth, then eat the rest. Don't burn yourself.
dish2_desc: Silken tofu in a numbing chile-bean sauce with ground pork. Sichuan's calling card.
dish3_desc: Thin wheat noodles in spicy sesame-chile sauce with crispy pork. Mix before eating.

name: Japan
cuisine_summary: Japanese food in SF is more than sushi — pork-bone ramen that took 12 hours, izakaya plates and beer with friends, and quietly precise omakase counters.
dish1_desc: Vinegared rice or pure fish, sliced by someone who's been doing it 20 years. Trust the chef.
dish2_desc: Pork bone broth simmered until milky, with chashu pork, soft egg, and chewy noodles.
dish3_desc: Vegetables and seafood in a crisp, lacy batter. Best straight from the fryer.

name: Korea
cuisine_summary: Korean food is fermented depth and tabletop fire — banchan side dishes that arrive before you order, soups that cure colds, and meat you grill yourself.
dish1_desc: Grill cuts like galbi (short rib) and samgyeopsal (pork belly) at your table; wrap in lettuce with rice and ssamjang.
dish2_desc: Rice bowl topped with sautéed vegetables, a fried egg, and gochujang — stir hard before eating.
dish3_desc: Stew of aged kimchi with pork or tuna. Sour, spicy, deeply restorative.

name: Thailand
cuisine_summary: Thai food balances four flavors at once — sweet, sour, salty, spicy. Curries built on pounded paste, stir-fried noodles with a smoky wok char, and herb-heavy salads.
dish1_desc: Wide rice noodles stir-fried with Chinese broccoli, egg, and dark soy. Less sweet than pad thai, more wok smoke.
dish2_desc: Coconut soup with chicken, galangal, lemongrass, and chile. Comforting and bright at the same time.
dish3_desc: Coconut milk curry of fresh green chiles, basil, and chicken or eggplant. Eat over jasmine rice.

name: Vietnam
cuisine_summary: Vietnamese food is bright, light, and full of herbs — rice noodle soups perfumed with star anise, baguette sandwiches from the French era, and a lot of lime.
dish1_desc: Beef noodle soup in long-simmered broth with star anise and clove. Add basil, sprouts, lime, chile to taste.
dish2_desc: Crusty baguette with pâté, pickled daikon and carrot, cucumber, cilantro, and meat. The Franco-Vietnamese sandwich.
dish3_desc: Spicy lemongrass beef noodle soup from central Vietnam — bolder and more pungent than phở.

name: India
cuisine_summary: Indian food is regional spice and technique — North Indian tandoor-charred breads and creamy curries, South Indian dosas crisp as paper, and biryani layered with saffron rice.
dish1_desc: Yogurt-marinated chicken in a tomato-cream sauce. Brit-Indian classic, weeknight favorite.
dish2_desc: Thin, crispy rice-and-lentil crepe wrapped around spiced potato. Eat with sambar and coconut chutney.
dish3_desc: Long-grain basmati rice layered with marinated meat, saffron, and fried onion. Special-occasion food.

name: Burma (Myanmar)
cuisine_summary: Burmese food sits at the crossroads of India, China, and Thailand — tea-leaf salads tossed at the table, coconut chicken noodle soup, and lots of crunchy fried bits.
dish1_desc: Fermented tea leaves tossed tableside with crunchy lentils, peanuts, sesame, cabbage, and lime. The dish to order first.
dish2_desc: Catfish-and-rice-noodle soup with lemongrass. The Burmese breakfast, eaten all day.
dish3_name: Coconut chicken noodle soup (ohn no khao swè)
dish3_desc: Yellow curry coconut broth with egg noodles and chicken. Garnish with fried onions, chile, lime, hard egg.

name: Philippines
cuisine_summary: Filipino food is bold and proudly sour — vinegar-braised meats, garlicky rice, and pork that fights with a fork. Plus halo-halo (lit. "mix-mix") for dessert.
dish1_desc: Chicken or pork braised in vinegar, soy, garlic, and bay. Every family has their version.
dish2_desc: Sizzling chopped pork (jowl + ear, classically) with onion, chile, and citrus. Eat with rice and a cold beer.
dish3_desc: Shaved ice with sweet beans, jellies, fruit, ube ice cream, and evaporated milk. Stir before eating.

name: Lebanon
cuisine_summary: Lebanese food is the mezze table — bowls of hummus and labneh, charred eggplant smoked over flame, and warm flatbread arriving in stacks.
dish1_desc: Smooth chickpea-tahini purée with lemon and good olive oil. Served warm, eaten with bread torn from the pile.
dish2_desc: Marinated meat shaved from a vertical spit, wrapped in flatbread with garlic sauce and pickles.
dish3_desc: Lentils and rice with deeply caramelized onions on top. Humble, perfect, vegetarian.

name: Yemen
cuisine_summary: Yemeni cooking is slow-roasted lamb and beef, smoky clay-oven breads, and side condiments that range from herbaceous to mouth-burning.
dish1_desc: Spiced rice with slow-roasted lamb or chicken cooked in a tandoor-like pit. Served on a communal platter.
dish2_desc: Brown meat stew topped with fenugreek froth, eaten with flatbread. Yemen's national dish.
dish3_desc: Flaky honey bread, layered with butter, drizzled with honey, dusted with black seed. Breakfast or anytime.

name: Israel
cuisine_summary: Israeli food draws from across the diaspora and the region — hummus shops with lifelong regulars, eggs poached in spiced tomato, and pita stuffed with falafel and pickles.
dish1_desc: Warm, mounded chickpea purée with olive oil, sometimes meat or whole chickpeas on top. Eaten with pita, not as a dip.
dish2_desc: Pita stuffed with fried eggplant, hard-boiled egg, hummus, tahini, amba (mango pickle), and herbs.
dish3_desc: Eggs poached in spiced tomato-pepper sauce. Breakfast for two, eaten straight from the pan with bread.

name: Ethiopia
cuisine_summary: Ethiopian food is communal — a big round of spongy sourdough flatbread (injera) topped with stews you tear off pieces to scoop up. Spice-heavy, no utensils.
dish1_desc: Chicken stew with berbere spice and hard-boiled egg, scooped with injera. The Sunday dish.
dish2_desc: Beef or lamb sautéed with onion, peppers, and rosemary. Crispy edges, tender center.
dish3_desc: Hand-minced raw beef seasoned with mitmita spice and clarified spiced butter. Eat with injera and ayib (mild cheese).
